title: Building Payments Already Made on a Claim — NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own)
content:
Claim payment ledger rule for the NFIP General Property Form and RCBAP Flood Policies (Write Your Own): the building payments already made that a new building payment is reduced by.

**Rule.** The building payments already made that a building payment is reduced by are settled as follows: when another claim number on the policy carries the same date of loss as a duplicate first notice, they are the building payments issued under both claim numbers less the building payment items voided under both; when there is no such duplicate first notice, building payment items on the claim have been voided and no building payment was issued on the claim after the latest void, they are all the building payments issued on the claim, because the voided item is reissued on its own under a new payment reference; otherwise they are the building payments issued on the claim less the building payment items voided on it.

## Truth table

| Duplicate first notice for the same date of loss | Building item voided on the claim | Building payment issued after the latest void | Payments already made |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | any | any | building payments under both claim numbers less voided items under both |
| no | yes | no | all building payments issued on the claim |
| no | yes | yes | building payments issued on the claim less voided items |
| no | no | — | building payments issued on the claim less voided items |

A payment issued on the same day as the latest void is not issued after it.

## Cases (hypothetical)

- Payments of 30,000.00 and 10,000.00 issued, the 10,000.00 item voided on 4 May, nothing issued since: 40,000.00 counts as already made, because the voided item is reissued on its own.
- The same, with a 10,000.00 reissue on 9 May: 50,000.00 issued in total, less 10,000.00 voided, is 40,000.00.
- A duplicate first notice for the same date of loss under a second claim number with 15,000.00 paid there and 30,000.00 here: 45,000.00.
